plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in a wide range of forms, from daisy-like to pompon and spider types. It thrives in the shortening days of fall and is prized in gardens and floral arrangements.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated across temperate regions of North America, Europe, and East Asia; native to China
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants that set buds only when nights grow long enough. In Japan, the flower is the emblem of the Imperial family and has its own festival, the Festival of Happiness.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, graceful tree covered in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers that often appear before the new leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere spring, entire streets are carpeted with fallen purple blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring (October to November in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), Argentina, and Brazil
plants.funFact: Pretoria in South Africa is known as the Jacaranda City because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, and local lore says a flower falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: A tall, airy annual with feathery foliage and delicate daisy-like flowers on slender stems. In mild-autumn climates it keeps blooming until the first hard frost and attracts pollinators late in the season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to late autumn (through October in mild Northern Hemisphere climates); spring in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to Mexico and the southwestern US; naturalized and cultivated worldwide
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word kosmos, meaning order or harmony, a name given by Spanish priests who grew the plants in their mission gardens in Mexico.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub that blooms in autumn, earlier than the common camellia. It bears fragrant, open flowers with prominent golden stamens against glossy dark green leaves, brightening the garden as other plants fade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to December in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Japan
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua leaves can be used to make tea, and its seeds are pressed into camellia oil, which is used in cooking, cosmetics, and hair care in Japan.
